Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. MoH (MINSAP Plan Strategique cholera 2009-2013, May 2009) explicitly tabulates zero cholera cases nationally and in every region for 1999-2001; its epidemic chronology (Fig. 3, Tableau 3) lists no epidemic between the 1997-98 epidemic (ended Jan 1998) and the 2002/2003 epidemic (first case December 2002, Bissau). Confidence downgraded from Level 1 band because (a) the same table shows artefactual zeros for 1995 and 2003 (WHO annual 119 and 290 cases; cross-year epidemics booked to their start year) - not applicable to 1999-2001 since no epidemic straddled those years, but it shows the table is epidemic-based; (b) PMC8583644 (metadata 16) attributes the 1998-2001 hole to 'the absence of reported cases during the periods of political instability and civil war... with consequent disruption of the already fragile health and surveillance systems'; (c) IDSR introduced only in 2004. Regional context: WHO WER annual reports 1999-2001 (metadata 24-26) do not list Guinea-Bissau; neighbour Guinea reported 546/44 (1999), 517/36 (2000), 392/22 (2001); Senegal not listed; WHO outbreak verification (largely media-based in 2001) recorded no Guinea-Bissau event. Agent 3 to re-validate. [AGENT 1 REVISION 2026-10-02] AGENT 1 corroboration: IRIN/OCHA 7 Sep 1999 (metadata 57) - MSF/MoH/WHO cholera detection and early-warning seminars held Aug 1999; MSF chronology 'Guinea-Bissau had cholera epidemics in 1986, 1987, 1994 and 1996-1997' (no epidemic since), i.e. active cholera preparedness/surveillance in 1999. (reason: Agent 1 Batch 3: corroborating source for 1999 absence)
